keyMessage.found: No one monitors network traffic or reads HIS and PACS logs, and vendor sessions are unlogged.
keyMessage.closes: Enable logging on HIS and PACS, deploy central logging, and agree a monitoring model.

categories.whatWorksToday: CCTV and door alarms cover restricted areas, and endpoint detection monitors the HIS and Active Directory servers.

strengths.statement: CCTV and door alarms are in place for restricted areas.
IT keeps a list of suppliers with remote access.
Endpoint detection and response monitors the HIS and Active Directory servers, and DMARC is configured for email.

gapFindings.title: Network traffic and server logs are not monitored
gapFindings.statement: No one watches network traffic or reads logs on the core systems, although the hospital runs around the clock.

supportingFacts.fact: Network traffic is not monitored with intrusion detection.
HIS and PACS produce no security logs.
Central logs for Microsoft 365 and Active Directory are not reviewed.
PACS servers have no endpoint protection.

extent.notChecked: Network device logs were not checked

gapFindings.consequence: An intruder works for days unseen, and ransomware is noticed only when files are encrypted.

likelihood.rationale: Monitoring is Poor on Criticality A systems and the threat is active.

ops.rationale: Undetected intruder stops or slows hospital operations.

fin.rationale: Undetected intruder adds recovery cost and revenue loss.

legal.rationale: Undetected intruder triggers reporting duties or regulator questions.

rep.rationale: Undetected intruder damages patient and public trust.

safety.rationale: Undetected intruder delays or disrupts patient care.

data.rationale: Undetected intruder exposes sensitive health records.

notApplicable.find: The affected systems or units are already identified.
notApplicable.exceptions: No system is known to be unable to meet the control.

gapFindings.title: Vendor sessions are unlogged and physical monitoring is unconfirmed
gapFindings.statement: CMC records neither vendor remote sessions nor proof that physical alerts are watched, so misuse leaves little trace.

supportingFacts.fact: Vendor remote access to HIS and PACS is not controlled or logged.
Vendor remote tools such as AnyDesk are not controlled.
CCTV and door alarms exist, but alert monitoring was only stated.

extent.notChecked: Monitoring of the hospital website vendor was not checked

gapFindings.consequence: A vendor or insider can copy patient records without detection, and CMC cannot prove what was accessed.

likelihood.rationale: Vendor access is Poor on Criticality A systems and no activity record is kept.

keyMessage.found: No rule turns an alert into an incident, and no detection covers ransomware precursors.
keyMessage.closes: Define triage steps and declaration criteria, then build ransomware detection rules.

gapFindings.title: No one triages alerts or declares incidents
gapFindings.statement: No team is assigned to analyze alerts, and no rule decides when an event becomes an incident.

supportingFacts.fact: No one is assigned to monitor security alerts.
Incident declaration criteria were not provided.
Alert information does not reach authorized staff.

extent.notChecked: Alert volume per day was not measured

gapFindings.consequence: Response starts late or not at all, and regulator clocks run before CMC declares an incident.

likelihood.rationale: No triage practice exists and the threat is active.

ops.rationale: Late declaration stops or slows hospital operations.

gapFindings.title: Ransomware precursors are not detected or correlated
gapFindings.statement: CMC probably has no rules for early ransomware signs, so the first visible sign is likely encrypted files.

supportingFacts.fact: No detection use cases were confirmed.
Information from multiple sources is not correlated.
The impact and scope of events are not estimated.

extent.notChecked: Endpoint rules on servers were not reviewed

gapFindings.consequence: Encryption spreads across servers before anyone reacts, and recovery starts from a full outage.

improvementActions.action: Enable security logs on HIS and PACS and deploy central logging for Criticality A systems
Agree a monitoring model, in-house or managed service, for 24 hour coverage
Install endpoint protection on the PACS servers
Log vendor remote sessions to HIS and PACS and review the logs weekly
Define alert triage steps and incident declaration criteria
Build detection rules for mass file renames, backup deletion, and new administrator accounts
